SELECTED_INDEX: 8
CONFIDENCE: 0.62
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is characteristic of a substituted benzene with strong ring modes and sulfonyl vibrations. Key matches: a strong ring breathing band near 1000 cm⁻¹ appears at 1033 cm⁻¹ (typical for para-disubstituted benzenes in Raman), aromatic C–H stretch at 3057 cm⁻¹ and strong ring C=C stretches at 1588 and ~1490 cm⁻¹ (GFQ-003). The pair at 1369/1386 cm⁻¹ and the band at 1176 cm⁻¹ are consistent with SO₂ asymmetric (~1320–1370) and symmetric (~1140–1180) stretches of a sulfonamide substituent, which candidate 8 uniquely contains. The intense 750 cm⁻¹ band aligns with an out-of-plane aromatic C–H deformation; its proximity to the nitro δ(NO₂) reference at ~752 cm⁻¹ (GFQ-022) supports the frequency region for heavy substituent ring deformations. Bands at 560 and 644 cm⁻¹ are compatible with ring/S–O/S–N deformations. Overall, candidate 8 (an anilide bearing a sulfonamide and benzylamine) best fits the observed aromatic and sulfonamide Raman features.
